newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors arrest ex-minister over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors arrest ex-minister over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors arrested a former cabinet minister and two members of parliament on Thursday in connection with a loans-for-kickbacks scandal swirling around the failed Hanbo Steel Co.

Those arrested were Kim Woo-suk, who resigned on Wednesday as Home Affairs minister, and lawmakers Hwang Byong-tai of the ruling New Korea Party and Kwon Roh-kap of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, a prosecution official said.
The three were all charged with bribery, the official said.

Thursday's arrest brings to eight the number of people jailed in connection with the scandal which has implicated several close associates of President Kim Young-sam and damaged his image as an anti-corruption reformer.
The president, who last month ordered a thorough probe into loans to Hanbo, has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, racked up $5.8 billion in loans before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
